**Deal notes added by Anders Holm 2026-08-26:**

Good call. Meat processor, 110 people, family owned, third generation, one site. Scorecard trigger from a retail customer, twelve products, deadline 15 October. Fifteen livestock suppliers, well within a manageable range, good energy records already collected for cost reasons which will translate directly to useful process data. Single point of contact, quality manager, MD approves quickly if the reasoning is clear.

Genuinely straightforward account on the substance. One thing I want on the record because it did not feel straightforward at all.

There was a third person on the call, Cecilia Rung, introduced only as "helping us with this" and never given a title or company. She said almost nothing for the whole thirty five minutes except two questions near the end, both about contract structure rather than about the product: whether the licence is per entity or per group, and whether a second company could be added to an existing agreement later at a rate rather than as a new contract.

Neither question is something a quality manager at a single site meat processor would normally think to ask. They are questions somebody asks when they are already thinking about more than one entity. I asked, lightly, whether she was working across a few companies, and got "a few things at once, generally," which told me nothing.

She was not on a visible consultant email address as far as I could tell from the call setup, and she did not behave like a consultant, a consultant usually asks about methodology to demonstrate expertise, she asked about contract mechanics instead. I do not know who she is or what she is helping with, and I think somebody should find out before this becomes a signed account, because the second company question in particular suggests there is a structure here nobody has told us about.

Proposal going out Thursday regardless, the deal itself stands on its own merits.
